task.description:
Design the fix for ISS-0459, building on ISSUE-FIXER's Step 1 diagnosis (read result.summary in full in the artifact above -- do not re-derive from scratch, but DO verify its central claim yourself against the cited letflow-queue source before designing on top of it, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.1). ISSUE-FIXER's finding, to verify then build on: letflow-queue's existing status:"blocked" (task.ex line 18, tasks.ex get_next_task SQL requiring status='open', tasks.ex tap_maybe_close_github_issue firing only on status=="done") already mechanically satisfies ISS-0459 Acceptance Criterion 1 today -- releasing a task with release_lock(status:"blocked") excludes it from all future get_next_task claims AND does not best-effort-close its GitHub issue. No new letflow-queue status value, no migration, no letflow-queue application code change was found necessary.

Your design must cover, as ONE coherent design even though it spans two repos:

1. DECIDE: does 'blocked' as the vocabulary word genuinely suffice, or is it risky enough (reads as 'stuck, needs action' vs the actual meaning 'investigated to a stable terminal stop, not a defect') that the design should instead propose a small letflow-queue enhancement -- e.g. an optional 'reason' or 'release_note' field stored alongside status, so a future reader of the queue's own data can distinguish 'this task is stuck because X is blocking it' from 'this task reached a genuine terminal non-fix verdict' without cross-referencing docs/issues/*.yaml by hand. Make a real design decision here, don't punt it back to ORCH -- but if you conclude a code change IS warranted, keep it minimal (e.g. one new nullable string column + one new optional request field) and scope it as an ADDITIVE, backward-compatible change (existing release_lock calls with no reason field must keep working unchanged).
2. Write the actual new prose for docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md's release_lock (#4) section: document the instrumented/no_defect -> release_lock(status:"blocked") convention explicitly, with the same rigor as the existing done/no-status distinction (ISS-0459 AC2) -- name it, define when to use it, state what it does NOT do (does not close GH issue, does not assert 'stuck'/'needs action'), and cross-reference ISSUE_QUEUE.md's resolved/instrumented/no_defect status vocabulary so a reader can map a WF-03 Step 5 local-status outcome to the correct release_lock call.
3. Also decide whether docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md needs a matching cross-reference addition (Step 5's own text) so a future ISSUE-FIXER reading THAT file alone still learns the correct release_lock call for instrumented/no_defect, not just TASK_QUEUE.md.
4. AC3 reconciliation: docs/issues/ISS-0458.yaml's queue task 458 was released with status:"done" (the ad-hoc, flagged-as-wrong workaround) for what was actually an instrumented outcome. Your design must state explicitly what ELIXIR-DEV/ORCH should do about task 458's current live state once the new mechanism/documentation exists -- e.g. re-release it as status:"blocked" to correct the record, or leave it (state why, if so). This does not require a letflow-queue code change to execute -- it's an operational release_lock call ORCH can make directly once the design is validated -- but the design must say so explicitly so nothing is silently skipped.
5. If (per point 1) you decide a letflow-queue code change IS warranted: write it as a design artefact under lib/letflow/design/ in THIS repo (interfaces/@spec/schema changes only, no implementation code, per this project's own design-artefact convention) describing the new column/field, the changeset change, and the release endpoint's new optional param -- ELIXIR-DEV will implement it in the SEPARATE letflow-queue repo directly from this design doc plus its own artifacts_in pointer, since letflow-queue does not have its own design-artefact pipeline (state this explicitly in your design doc's own preamble, so ELIXIR-DEV knows to treat it as instructive spec, not a literal file to copy into letflow-queue's tree).
6. If (per point 1) you decide documentation-only is correct and no code change is warranted: state that explicitly and do not produce a design artefact under lib/letflow/design/ for a code change that isn't happening -- write your reasoning into this handoff's own result.summary instead, and route Step 3 directly to the TASK_QUEUE.md/ISSUE_QUEUE.md doc edits.

Do NOT write the actual TASK_QUEUE.md/ISSUE_QUEUE.md edits yourself as committed file changes in this step -- draft the exact prose in this handoff's result.summary (or a design artefact) for CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to review, then ELIXIR-DEV applies it at Step 3.
acceptance_criteria: ISSUE-FIXER's core finding (blocked status already satisfies AC1 mechanically) is independently re-verified against the cited letflow-queue source, not merely copied
A clear, justified decision is made: documentation-only fix, OR a minimal additive letflow-queue schema/API change -- not left ambiguous
If documentation-only: exact TASK_QUEUE.md release_lock section prose is drafted, meeting ISS-0459 AC2's rigor bar (same level of detail as the existing done/no-status distinction)

If a code change is proposed: a design artefact exists under lib/letflow/design/ with interfaces/@spec/schema only, no implementation code, and explicitly states it targets the separate letflow-queue repo
ISSUE_QUEUE.md cross-reference need is explicitly assessed (add or explicitly justify not adding)
AC3 (task 458 reconciliation) has an explicit, actionable recommendation in the design, not left for a later run to figure out
No committed edits to TASK_QUEUE.md, ISSUE_QUEUE.md, or letflow-queue source in this step -- design/draft only

result.summary:
VERIFICATION (independently re-derived, not copied from ISSUE-FIXER's summary). Read letflow-queue source directly this run:
- task.ex:18 `@statuses ~w(open done blocked)` CONFIRMED live. release_lock's own independent guard at tasks.ex:351 (`status not in [nil, "open", "done", "blocked"] -> {:error, :invalid_status}`) enforces the identical three-value vocabulary a second time.
- tasks.ex:174-204 `get_next_task`'s claim UPDATE: both the issue-type subquery (line 176-189) and the requirement-type subquery (line 190-204) filter `WHERE t.status = 'open' AND t.locked_by IS NULL AND ...`. A row with status='blocked' cannot satisfy either COALESCE branch. CONFIRMED: permanently ineligible for claim until a future release_lock/set_lock call explicitly writes it back to 'open'.
- tasks.ex:382-401 `tap_maybe_close_github_issue/2`: the GitHub-closing clause pattern-matches literal `"done"` on BOTH the task's post-update `status` field and the `status` argument (line 383-386); the catch-all clause at line 401 (`tap_maybe_close_github_issue(result, _status), do: result`) is a pure passthrough for every other value, "blocked" included. CONFIRMED: release_lock(status:"blocked") never calls GitHub.close_issue/1.

ISSUE-FIXER's central claim is verified first-hand, not merely trusted: today, with zero letflow-queue code change, release_lock(status:"blocked") mechanically satisfies ISS-0459 AC1 (excluded from all future get_next_task claims; does not best-effort-close the GitHub issue).

DECISION (point 1): DOCUMENTATION-ONLY. No letflow-queue schema/API change in this fix.
Reasoning: The three mechanical requirements of AC1 are already met by the existing 'blocked' status with no code change, verified above. The semantic-mismatch risk ISSUE-FIXER raised is real and I independently agree with it -- 'blocked' as a bare English word overwhelmingly reads as "stuck, needs action," which is backwards from "investigated to a stable terminal stop." But the task's own instructions are explicit that this risk, if present, should route to a proposed follow-on enhancement rather than gating this documentation fix on a letflow-queue code change -- and I agree with that framing on the merits, for three reasons: (a) the risk is a readability/foot-gun risk, not a correctness risk -- the mechanism works regardless of how well-named it is; (b) the fix for a readability risk is precise documentation that names the convention explicitly and warns against the collision, which this design supplies below, and that fix ships today with zero deploy/migration risk to a live, deployed service; (c) inventing a schema change (a nullable `release_reason`/`status_reason` column plus a new optional release_lock request field) is a reasonable idea but is speculative extra surface on a service with a deliberately minimal "four operations, on purpose" design ethos (TASK_QUEUE.md line ~118, letflow-queue's own README "Design" section) -- adding a field should be justified by an actual future collision (two different 'blocked' releases meaning different things, discovered as a real incident), not pre-emptively. I am filing that enhancement as a separate, non-blocking follow-on issue recommendation (see below) rather than a code-change design artefact in this run, per the task's own point 6 branch. No `lib/letflow/design/` artefact is produced by this run, because no code change is happening.

FOLLOW-ON ISSUE RECOMMENDATION (not filed by this design step -- CODE-DESIGNER does not call register_task; this is a recommendation for ORCH to file via ISSUE_QUEUE.md's normal procedure once this design is validated, severity MINOR, tags [queue-protocol, process]): "letflow-queue's release_lock status vocabulary (open/done/blocked) has no sub-reason field distinguishing a genuinely-stuck/actionable 'blocked' from an instrumented/no_defect terminal 'blocked' -- consider an additive nullable `status_reason` (or `release_note`) string column plus an optional `status_reason` request field on POST /tasks/:id/release, populated only when the caller wants to record why, existing callers unaffected." This is exactly the shape point 1 described (one nullable column, one optional param, additive/backward-compatible) if a future incident shows the bare word actually causing confusion in practice.

DRAFTED TASK_QUEUE.md PROSE (section 4, release_lock) -- to be inserted immediately after the existing "status: done" paragraph (ending "...or delivered requirement, not an investigation, partial finding, or reverted attempt.") and before the two ```bash examples, at the same heading level, meeting ISS-0459 AC2's rigor bar (same level of detail as the existing done/no-status distinction):

---
**`status: "blocked"` means the run reached a genuine, stable terminal stop that is NOT a resolution — use it for a WF-03 Step 5 outcome recorded as `instrumented` or `no_defect` (see `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md`'s "Issue status vocabulary").** Both of those statuses assert the run investigated the issue to completion and reached a real, evidence-backed verdict, but neither asserts the underlying defect was fixed — `instrumented` ships verified diagnostic work with the root cause still open (and a required `superseded_by:` pointer); `no_defect` establishes there was no root cause to remove. Releasing either outcome with `status: "done"` is wrong for the same reason bare no-status release is wrong for a hand-back: it either falsely claims resolution (`"done"`'s documented meaning, above) or leaves the task `open` and immediately re-claimable by the very next `get_next_task` call — for `task_type: "issue"` tasks specifically, `get_next_task`'s LIFO issue-priority claim order (see function 2, above) means an `open`, already-fully-investigated issue-type task is re-claimed ahead of every other open task, producing a re-selection loop for any automated session that doesn't special-case it (this is exactly what happened live, 2026-09-04, to queue task 458/ISS-0458 — see that record's own account).

`status: "blocked"` avoids both failure modes: it excludes the task from every future `get_next_task` eligibility check (the claim query filters `WHERE t.status = 'open'` only — a `blocked` row can never match), so there is no re-selection loop, and it does NOT best-effort-close the task's linked GitHub Issue (only a release whose resulting status is literally `"done"` triggers that; `"blocked"` is a pure passthrough) — appropriate, since an `instrumented`/`no_defect` outcome typically still wants the GitHub issue's own Step 5 close-with-comment procedure to run on its own terms (see `WF-03_issue_resolving.md` Step 5), not the queue's best-effort side-closure.

**What `status: "blocked"` does NOT assert:** despite the English word's ordinary sense ("stuck, waiting on something, needs action" — the same sense this doc itself uses at "report blocked, do not select," above), a queue task released with `status: "blocked"` under this convention is NOT necessarily stuck or actionable. It means "terminally stopped, not resolved" — a deliberately reused existing enum value, not a new state invented for this meaning. Do not read `status: "blocked"` in queue task listings as "this needs attention" without also checking the linked `docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml` record's own `status:` field (`instrumented` or `no_defect`) for what it actually means; the queue's bare three-value status field cannot distinguish a genuinely-stuck-and-actionable task from a genuinely-terminal one on its own today.

```bash
# Releasing an instrumented/no_defect WF-03 outcome:
curl -X POST https://queue-test.ai-dala.com/tasks/42/release \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $QUEUE_AUTH_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"agent_id": "'"$HOSTNAME"'-orch", "status": "blocked"}'
```
---

ISSUE_QUEUE.md CROSS-REFERENCE DECISION (point 3): YES, add. Reasoning: ISSUE_QUEUE.md's "Issue status vocabulary" section is the canonical definition site TASK_QUEUE.md's new prose above points back to, and its own worked examples (ISS-0109, ISS-0200) already establish the pattern of teaching the queue-consequence alongside the status definition. A future ISSUE-FIXER or ORCH landing on ISSUE_QUEUE.md first (the more likely entry point when closing out a WF-03 run, since Step 5 itself points there) should not have to separately discover TASK_QUEUE.md's release_lock section to learn the correct call. Concretely, two insertions:

(a) Append one sentence to the end of the existing `instrumented` bullet (after "...file that successor before transitioning the record. State plainly in the record what the shipped work does not close."):
"Release the queue task with `release_lock(status: \"blocked\")`, not `\"done\"` and not no-status — see `TASK_QUEUE.md`'s release_lock section for why."

(b) Append the same sentence, adapted, to the end of the existing `no_defect` bullet's evidence-bar paragraph (after its closing sentence about `verdict_at:`):
"Release the queue task with `release_lock(status: \"blocked\")`, not `\"done\"` and not no-status — see `TASK_QUEUE.md`'s release_lock section for why."

(No change needed to the `resolved` bullet — that outcome already correctly uses `release_lock(status: "done")` per Step 5's existing text.)

WF-03_issue_resolving.md STEP 5 FINDING (surfaced during design, not originally scoped to this handoff's owned_modules, but must not be silently dropped): Step 5's own text at line 206-213 currently instructs, unconditionally on "this step's PASS": call `release_lock` with `status: "done"` — with NO branch for `instrumented`/`no_defect` outcomes. This is the actual proximate cause of ISS-0458's ad-hoc `status:"done"` workaround: the run's own procedural instructions told it to release with "done" regardless of which terminal status Step 5 §1 had just written. Fixing only TASK_QUEUE.md/ISSUE_QUEUE.md's prose (this design's scope) documents the correct convention but does not correct the instruction that produces the wrong call by default. RECOMMENDATION: this line needs a status-conditional rewrite (`resolved` -> `release_lock(status: "done")`; `instrumented`/`no_defect` -> `release_lock(status: "blocked")`), mirroring the branching structure Step 5 §2 already uses for its GitHub close-comment text three lines above it. `docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md` is NOT in this handoff's `owned_modules` (only TASK_QUEUE.md/ISSUE_QUEUE.md are) and I have made no edit to it. I recommend ORCH route a small follow-on edit to that file (either as an in-scope addition to this same fix's Step 3, widening owned_modules, or as its own tiny follow-on task) rather than leaving Step 5 instructing every future run to make ISS-0458's same mistake. Flagging explicitly so this isn't silently skipped.

AC3 RECONCILIATION (point 4) -- explicit, actionable recommendation: RE-RELEASE queue task 458 as `status: "blocked"` to correct the live record, once this design is validated and the TASK_QUEUE.md/ISSUE_QUEUE.md prose above is merged (so the convention is documented before/at the same time it's applied, not applied silently ahead of its own documentation). Reasoning: ISS-0458.yaml's own resolution_note already states plainly that the `status:"done"` release was "a workaround, not a fix" and "should not be treated as settled practice" -- the record itself flags this as wrong. Task 458 is currently `open`+unlocked at the letflow-queue level with the GitHub issue #882 already closed (best-effort, harmless-idempotent side effect of the "done" release) -- re-releasing with `status:"blocked"` is safe to execute: it does not reopen or re-close the GitHub issue (only a transition TO "done" triggers the close call; there is no matching "reopen on non-done" behavior in tasks.ex, confirmed by reading tap_maybe_close_github_issue/2 above -- it only ever acts on the "done" match arm), it only flips the queue's own status field and clears any stale lock. Concretely: `release_lock(id: 458, status: "blocked")` (task is already unlocked, so `agent_id` can be any current value or the call can use `force: true` if the no-agent-id-required path is preferred -- either is safe since the task holds no live lock to conflict with). This is an operational release_lock call, not a code change -- ORCH can execute it directly once this design is validated; it should NOT be executed by this design step itself (out of scope per the handoff's own "design/draft only" boundary) and should not be silently left undone -- I am stating it explicitly here per the task's own instruction so Step 3/ORCH picks it up rather than it falling through.

SUMMARY OF WHAT STEP 3 (ELIXIR-DEV) SHOULD DO: (1) apply the TASK_QUEUE.md release_lock-section prose drafted above, verbatim or lightly copy-edited; (2) apply the two ISSUE_QUEUE.md cross-reference sentences drafted above; (3) no letflow-queue source changes; no lib/letflow/design/ artefact (none produced by this step). ORCH, once Step 3 merges: (4) re-release queue task 458 with status:"blocked" per the AC3 recommendation above; (5) consider filing the WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 branching-fix as a small follow-on (flagged above, currently un-actioned); (6) consider filing the optional letflow-queue status_reason follow-on enhancement recommendation above as a new MINOR issue via the normal ISSUE_QUEUE.md procedure, non-blocking.
